rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers came at night so Jacob would not read their faces in daylight; a saying likewise counsels seeking favors by night and avoiding daytime apologies.
rows.anchor: في ظلمة الليل لئلا يتفرس أبيهم في وجوههم إذا رآها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their tears do not establish truth, since crying can be feigned; crying is the flow of tears from the eye in sadness.
rows.anchor: والآية دالة على أن البكاء لا يدل على الصدق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They claim they raced, left Joseph with their belongings, and the wolf ate him; they concede Jacob will not believe them even if truthful.
rows.anchor: إنا ذهبنا نستبق وتركنا يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They knew Jacob would doubt them because of his clear insight, their suspicious behavior, and the telltale signs of a lie; they had never been caught lying.
rows.anchor: لا يصدقهم من وجوه منها ما هو عليه من صحة الفراسة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the brothers slaughtered a young ewe and smeared its blood on Joseph's shirt as fabricated evidence.
rows.anchor: نقله الرماني عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما وعن مجاهد

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid is also cited for the account that the brothers used a slaughtered ewe's blood to falsify Joseph's death.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما وعن مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blood is called a lie because their claim that it was Joseph's blood contradicted reality; blood is a red, flowing substance normally found in animal veins.
rows.anchor: أي مكذوب , أطلق عليه المصدر مبالغة لأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unattributed report says Jacob threw the shirt over his face and cried until its blood stained him, remarking that he had never seen such a gentle wolf.
rows.anchor: وروي أن يعقوب عليه الصلاة والسلام أخذ القميص منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shirt serves as three signs: proof the brothers lied, proof Joseph was truthful when his shirt was torn from behind, and a means by which his father's sight returned.
rows.anchor: وكان القميص ثلاث آيات : دلالته على كذبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob did not press them for Joseph's remains: a wolf normally leaves some prey, but asking could provoke worse harm; his later instruction to search for Joseph supports this.
rows.anchor: من الشرور أكثر مما جاؤوا به من المحذور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob says their souls embellished and made their deed seem easy; beautiful patience means enduring without complaining to people, while God is the one asked for help against their account.
rows.anchor: أي زينت وسهلت , من السول وهو الاسترخاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers are not thereby hypocrites: breaking promises, lying, and betraying trust occurred once, whereas hypocrisy makes them habitual or predominant.
rows.anchor: ولا يقال : إنهم بهذا أجمعوا أوصاف المنافق ( إذا وعد أخلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lexical permutations of sawl and sayl cluster around desired aims and their attendant senses, including longing, adornment, ease, deception, treatment, persistence, comfort, and hardship.
rows.anchor: تدوران على ما يطمع فيه من المراد , ويلزمه رغد العيش والزينة

rows.speaker: القزاز
rows.claim: Al-Qazzaz says wasila can mean rank or position with a king; the passage also gives it the senses of a need and seeking access.
rows.anchor: قال القزاز : وقيل : توسلت وتوصلت - بمعنى , والوسيلة : الحاجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After denying worldly means of help on Judgment Day, the passage identifies God as sole sovereign; creation of the vast heavens and earth proves his power, uniqueness, and ability to resurrect.
rows.anchor: وهما أكبر خلقا منكم وأعظم شأنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain revives dead, dry land and produces fruit as sustenance, providing an analogy and evidence for raising the dead.
rows.anchor: بعد يبس الأرض وجفاف نباتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God subjects ships to sail by his command and also subjects rivers; their movement across the sea is a marvel to reason.
rows.anchor: بأمره } ولما كانت الأنهار من النعم الكبار

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummani defines dāʾibayn as two things continuously carrying on their accustomed work; the sun and moon's motion and light bring benefits such as heating and ripening.
rows.anchor: والدؤوب : مرور الشيء في العمل على عادة جارية فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun signifies daytime and the moon nighttime; each repeatedly follows the other, since perpetual day or night would disrupt plant and animal life.
rows.anchor: لو كان أحدهما سرمدا لاختل الحال بعدم النبات والحيوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave people everything they ask for in the sense of what they need, which they ask for potentially; naming the gift directs people from its effects to its giver.
rows.anchor: أي ما أنتم محتاجون إليه فأنتم سائلوه بالقوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People cannot enumerate or fully know God's blessings: even one blessing exceeds counting, whether by number or the pebbles Arabs used for counting.
rows.anchor: لا تحيطوا بها ولا تعرفوا عد الحصى المقابلة لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Freedom from every bodily illness in medical books, and from every false creed or deviation in the mind, are each blessings beyond human enumeration.
rows.anchor: السلامة من كل داء ذكره الأطباء في كتبهم - على كثرتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse recalls the opening claim that everything in heaven and earth belongs to God, establishing that nothing can equal him and no one can bargain with him on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: فهذا شرح قوله أول السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chapter focuses on disbelievers who neglect prophetic guidance despite its blessings; humans are intensely unjust and ungrateful when they fail to thank God and instead disbelieve.
rows.anchor: حيث يهمل الشكر , ويتعداه إلى الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Naḥl ends with forgiveness and mercy because it is a chapter of blessings: its opening forbids rushing punishment, since God delays people and lets them enjoy benefits.
rows.anchor: وختم مثل ذلك في سورة النحل ب { غفور رحيم } لأن تلك سورة النعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lasting good deeds surpass transient wealth and children in this life and the next; their reward remains and prospects rise, while worldly possessions fail when most needed.
rows.anchor: خير من المال والبنين في العاجل والآجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reward is better with the Lord, who knows outcomes, and the hope associated with it is better than hope invested in money and children.
rows.anchor: لأن ثوابها إلى بقاء , وأملها كل ساعة في تحقيق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing worldly life and its passing, the passage turns to the Day of Gathering, whose disgrace, poverty, and confinement are especially feared by the great-hearted.
rows.anchor: فكيف إذا انضم إليه الفقر فيكف إذا صاحبهما الحبس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains are moved by God's power and the earth is laid bare of caves, fissures, mountains, plants, trees, and shade; all creatures are gathered before the mountains move.
rows.anchor: لا غار فيها ولا صدع ولا جبل ولا نبت ولا شجر ولا ظل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gathering exposes hidden and shameful things, and judgment reaches even the smallest matter; everyone witnesses the mountains' collapse and structures' destruction.
rows.anchor: الموقف الذي ينكشف فيه المخبآت , وتظهر الفضائح والمغيبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one is left out of the gathering, since God is neither distracted nor incapable.
rows.anchor: لأنه لا ذهول ولا عجز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses's experience of forgetting and later being guided, his prayer for eloquence, and his plea for a helper model the Prophet's prayer for a minister; God aided him through Umar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb.
rows.anchor: فأيده بأعظم ويزير : عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The completion of Moses's story rebukes Jews who taught Quraysh to ask Muhammad about the Spirit: it includes details unknown to them, such as the festival day, magicians' faith, threatened crucifixion, and the Samaritan's use of the messenger's trace.
rows.anchor: منها أن الموعد كان يوم الزينة , ومنها إيمان السحرة

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr explains that after Mary names blessed prophets and warns of corrupt successors, the prospect might alarm Muhammad, so the next surah reassures him that the Qur'an was not sent to make him miserable.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر بن الزبير في بر هانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maryam closes by recalling destroyed generations after warning a stubborn people; seeing Quraysh resist made the Prophet grieve, and God reassures him that revelation was not sent to burden him.
rows.anchor: وأيضا فقد ختمت سورة مريم يقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's grief reflected fear that Quraysh would not respond and his labor would be prolonged; receptive people who fear God will respond when reminded and shown God's signs.
rows.anchor: فيطول العناء والمشقة , فبشره سبحانه وتعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reassurance parallels the command not to let their words grieve him, then is followed by mention of the All-Merciful established over the Throne.
rows.anchor: كما قيل له في موضع آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second coherence reading is stronger: creation belongs to God, and a divinely aided person can face no difficult task; Moses's rescue, Pharaoh's destruction, and Israel's emergence reinforce this point.
rows.anchor: وهذا الوجه الثاني أولى من الأول - والله أعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Returning from Midian, Moses clearly saw a fire in the dark and told his family to stay; anastu denotes seeing plainly, and he hoped to bring a glowing brand for warmth or find guidance on the hidden road.
rows.anchor: أي أبصرت في هذا الظلام إبصارا بينا لا شبهة فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A qabas is a flame carried on the tip of a stick, useful against the cold; hudā means guidance because the path had become hidden.
rows.anchor: أي بشعلة من النار في رأس حطبة فيها جمرة تعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive 'he was called' first conceals the caller and then magnifies the summons when Moses is named.
rows.anchor: ولما كان في الإبهام ثم تعيين تشويق ثم تعظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Abu Hafs read the clause with the preposition omitted and a fatḥa; other readers understand an implied verb of saying.
rows.anchor: مسقطا الجار في قراءة ابن كثير وأبي عمرو وأبي حفص بالفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses is told to remove his sandals as courtly etiquette, to receive their blessing, and to settle without turning back toward family; dream interpreters take footwear to signify a child.
rows.anchor: كما يفعل بحضرات الملوك أدبا , ولتنالك بركتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sacred valley is purified of what is unfit for a king's court; the wording also indicates that God is not contained by place or time.
rows.anchor: أي المطهر عن كل ما لا يليق بأفنية الملوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God chose Moses as a prophet and instructed him to listen with focused attention; the private, intimate-sounding address signals his honor even though it is heard openly.
rows.anchor: أي أنصت ملقيا سمعك معملا قلبك للسماع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge of God is the first obligation; the name Allah gathers the meanings of the divine names, and only God fully bears their perfection, so worship belongs to him alone.
rows.anchor: فذكر الاسم العلم لأن هذا مقامه إذ الأنسب للملطوف به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer is the highest rite and the religion's core because constant remembrance sustains mindfulness and wards off evil; it joins divine majesty and beauty.
rows.anchor: لأنها أعلى شرائعه لأنها حاملة على المراقبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hour will certainly come to end purposeless creation and make justice visible; its time is concealed so people remain alert, since it may arrive suddenly at any moment.
rows.anchor: فراقبني فإن الأمر يكون بغتة , ما من لحظة إلا وهي صالحة للترقب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every soul will be recompensed for what it does, however slight its actions or however persistent its striving.
rows.anchor: أي توجد من السعي في كل وقت كما يفعل من أمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's purpose is to prove the Hour's certainty and nearness, even through death, and the judgment of both eminent and lowly; the unique Creator cannot be prevented and does not alter his promise.
rows.anchor: مقصودها الاستدلال على تحقق الساعة وقربها ولو بالموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The combined prophetic stories provide the proof: no single story independently establishes every aspect, but each points to part of it.
rows.anchor: ولا يستقل قصة منها استقلالا ظاهرا بجميع ذلك كما سنبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder from God is unmistakably divine admonition, but God did not make the heavens and earth as idle play; worldly distractions and hardships show creation serves another purpose.
rows.anchor: لكنا لم نرد ذلك فلم يكن

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī distinguishes ʿinda for what appears outwardly from ladun for what is inward; here the latter denotes God's hidden, special presence.
rows.anchor: وخص الحرالي { عند } بما ظهر , و { لدن } بما بطن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular 'heaven' suits the immediate context of people denying resurrection, while other contexts call the heavens plural.
rows.anchor: فوحد السماء هنا وجمعها في غير هذا الموضع لاقتضاء الحال ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God casts the revealed, steadfast Qur'anic truth against falsehood as a solid rock against a hollow body, smashing falsehood and making it vanish immediately.
rows.anchor: تصويرا للحق بجعل الحق كأنه جرم صلب كالصخرة قذف بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an contains argument and firmness, with no frivolity or falsehood; it destroys the falsehood people invent about it and other matters.
rows.anchor: هذا الذكر الحكيم الذي أنزلناه جدال كله وثباتا جميعه لا لهو فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Woe is due for describing everything according to whim without divine warrant, since people do not grasp realities; truth exposes false descriptions of the Qur'an, God, and the world.
rows.anchor: من وصفكم لكل شيء بما تهوى أنفسكم من غير إذن منا لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything in the heavens and earth belongs to God, proving rationally that he owns and rules all creation.
rows.anchor: فدل ذلك دلالة عقلية على أنه مالك الكل وملكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the angels those 'with him' signifies honored closeness like a king's favored attendants, not spatial proximity; they do not act arrogantly or tire of worship.
rows.anchor: تمثيلا بما نعرف من أصفياء الملوك عند التعبير بعند من مجرد القرب في المكانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels glorify God continually by words and deeds through every part of night and day, never ceasing.
rows.anchor: دائما . ولما لم يصرح هنا بإنكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike Fussilat, this passage does not explicitly mention denial or its accompanying arrogance, so it does not add emphasis or a conjunction to the angels' denial of weariness.
rows.anchor: بخلاف ما في { فصلت } فإن الأمر فيها مبني على حد استكبارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything other than God is beneath the rank of the one possessing all perfection; worship is merited by chosen action, not by compelled natural behavior.
rows.anchor: كل ما سوى الله دنه , نبه على ذلك بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated 'what' makes clear that the idol neither causes any harm nor can block benefit, and does not benefit or avert harm; blame does not require absence of both qualities together.
rows.anchor: ولو أسقطت ( ما ) من الثاني لظن أن الذم يشترط فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling on a powerless object is gross folly and remote misguidance: leaving its worship cannot stop God's beneficence, and worship cannot secure benefit from it or avert harm.
rows.anchor: لأن الأول لو ترك عبادته ما قدر على منع إحسانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The supposed patron has no power over either harm or benefit; even under the hypothetical that it could act, harm is more likely than benefit, making it a wretched patron and companion.
rows.anchor: ليس مرجو النفع كما هو مخشي الضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone can choose and bring about either benefit or harm; he admits believers who do good deeds to gardens with rivers flowing beneath them.
rows.anchor: أي من أي مكان أردت من أرضها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers' worldly harms and defects serve to purify their lapses and errors; God's action follows whatever he wills.
rows.anchor: تطهيرا لهم مما اقترفوه من الزلات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lot's people were destroyed immediately after his escape; the word 'then' rhetorically stages the event, while 'the others' conveys that they lagged in every respect.
rows.anchor: أهلكنا هلاكا بغتة صلبا أصم في غاية النكد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rain is explicitly against them, marking it as punishment; it was a terrible rain for a people whom Lot had warned.
rows.anchor: أي ما أسوأ مطر الذين خوفهم لوط عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrasting fates of the deniers and those saved are a clear sign of the messengers' warnings and promises; later peoples knew their accounts and observed their ruins.
rows.anchor: علموا أخبارهم , وضموا إلى بعض الأخبار نظر الديار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people after those nations still did not believe, despite knowing their history and seeing their traces.
rows.anchor: وما كان أكثرهم مؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone is mighty in punishing enemies and merciful in favoring allies; his mercy also includes sending messengers and clarifying difficult matters even for enemies.
rows.anchor: في لطفه بأوليائه , ورفقه بأعدائه بإرسال الرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of the dense, water-absorbing grove rejected Shuʿayb and thereby rejected all messengers; he was sent with a heavenly miracle that challengers could not match.
rows.anchor: لتكذيبهم شعيبا عليه السلام فيما أتى به من المعجزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuʿayb is not called their brother because he was a city dweller addressing pastoral people; the passage says prophets were sent from towns, honoring settled communities for their shared wisdom and blessing.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل : أخوهم , إشارة إلى أنه لم يرسل نبيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqwa means fear of God, which is what Shuʿayb commands when asking whether they will not be reverent.
rows.anchor: تكونون من أهل التقو , وهو مخافة من الله سبحانه وتعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuʿayb identifies himself as a trustworthy messenger from God, without fraud or betrayal, who faithfully conveys all that was revealed to him.
rows.anchor: لا غش عندي ولا خداع ولا خيانه , فلذلك أبلغ جميع ما أرسلت به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He calls them to fear God and obey him because his sincerity is established, and because God has favored them with the grove and other gifts.
rows.anchor: المحسن إليكم بهذه الغيضة وغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuʿayb asks no payment so as not to repel them; his reward is from the Lord of all, the only benefactor who needs no one while all depend on him.
rows.anchor: فأنا لا أرجوا أبدا أحدا يحتاج إلى الإحسان إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All messengers agree in calling people to fear, obey, and worship God sincerely, while showing counsel, integrity, honesty, and restraint from seeking payment.
rows.anchor: اتضح أن الرسل متطابقون في الدعوة في الأمر بالتقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root problem is greed for money; sellers must fully measure for customers just as they expect full measure for themselves.
rows.anchor: إذا كلتم كما توفونه إذا اكتلتم لأنفسكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not become a settled class of short-changers: cheating others impoverishes one's own religion, though passing impulses can be resisted and erased.
rows.anchor: أي كونا هو كالجبلة , ولعله إشارة إلى ما يعرض من نحو ذلك من الخواطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Give full weight on a perfectly upright scale; separating the command about weighing from measuring highlights its importance.
rows.anchor: ولم يجمعهما لما للتفريق من التعريف بمزيد الاهتمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not diminish people's property in measure, weight, or any other way, and do not spread corruption more broadly by acting without reflection.
rows.anchor: في كيل أو وزن أو غيرهما نقصا يكون كالسبخة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear the Creator, who can destroy you with ease, and the powerful ancient peoples; even fellow Arabs like ʿĀd had enormous strength and bodily toughness.
rows.anchor: الذين كانوا على خلقه وطبيعة عظيمة كأنها الجبال

none: Verse text only; no commentary is included in this segment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage quotes the Torah's account that Jacob's twelve sons entered Egypt, numbering seventy including Joseph, and that their descendants multiplied greatly after Joseph and his generation died.
rows.anchor: ذكر المضمون هذا من التوراة : قال في و السفر الثاني منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A new Pharaoh, unaware of Joseph, feared Israel's growth and imposed harsh forced labor, using them to build store cities including Pithom and Raamses.
rows.anchor: فملك على مصر ملك جديد لم يكن يعرفيوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh ordered Hebrew midwives Puah and Shiphrah to kill newborn boys and spare girls; they feared God, disobeyed, and said Hebrew women gave birth before a midwife arrived.
rows.anchor: التي تسمى إحداهما فوعا والخرى شوفرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Torah says God treated the midwives well and gave them households; Pharaoh then ordered every Hebrew boy thrown in the river while girls were spared.
rows.anchor: فأحسن اله إلى القابلتين لصنعهما هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Levite couple hid their attractive newborn son for three months, then placed him in a pitch-coated wooden basket in the river shallows while his sister watched.
rows.anchor: فأخذت تابوتا من خشب الصنوبر , وطلته بالقار والزفت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's daughter found the crying child while bathing, felt compassion, and drew him from the water.
rows.anchor: فخرجت بنت فرعون تغتسل في النهر , فنظرت إلى التابوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Torah account says the child's sister arranged for his mother to nurse him for Pharaoh's daughter; later the princess adopted and named him Moses because she drew him from water.
rows.anchor: فأخذت المرأة الغلام فأرضعته فشب الغلام فأتت به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As an adult Moses killed an Egyptian who was beating a Hebrew, then the next day rebuked a Hebrew disputant, who exposed the killing; Pharaoh sought him, so Moses fled to Midian.
rows.anchor: فقتل المصري , فمات ودفنه في الرمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At Midian Moses rescued and watered the seven daughters of Reuel, was invited to eat, married Zipporah, and had a son named Eliezer.
rows.anchor: فاستقى لنا الماء , وسقى غنمنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that both disputants were Hebrews should be aligned with the Qur'an if possible; otherwise the Torah account was altered.
rows.anchor: إن أمكن تنزيل ما في القرآن عليه فذاك , وإلا فهو مما بدلوه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari supports the Torah's statement that Shuʿayb had seven daughters by identifying the two women in the Qur'anic account, though the author says that identification is not necessary.
rows.anchor: الزمخشري بتعيينهما بقوله ( هاتين )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses completed the full agreed term and fulfilled all the work he had promised his father-in-law.
rows.anchor: أن التقدير : فلما التزم موسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: أبو ذر رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: A report raised to the Prophet and transmitted by al-Ṭabarānī from Abu Dharr says Moses completed the more complete of the two terms.
rows.anchor: روى الطبراني في الوسط معناه عن أبي ذر رضي الله عنه مرفوعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses appears to have remained with his father-in-law after the term, since the coordinated phrase 'and he traveled' is not the direct result of 'when he completed.'
rows.anchor: لأنه عطف بالواو قوله : { وسار }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anasa means that Moses saw the fire; its light cheered him, and he needed both directions and warmth.
rows.anchor: آنسته رؤيتها وشرحته إنارتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He tells his family to stay, using the masculine plural by grammatical precedence and because sons may also have accompanied him; the wording emphasizes that women should be sheltered.
rows.anchor: ولما كان النساء أعظم ما ينبغي ستره , أطلق عليها ضمير الذكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He emphasizes seeing a fire because a flame in a remote, cold place at that time seems unlikely.
rows.anchor: لاستبعاد أن يكون في ذلك المكان القفر وفي ذلك الوقت الشديد البرد نار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His tentative 'perhaps' expresses humility, the surah's intended quality; a thick branch with embers might provide useful directions or warmth.
rows.anchor: ولذا عبر بالجذوة التي مدار مادتها الثبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laʿallakum taṣṭalūn means hoping to draw near and warm themselves at the fire, indicating a winter night.
rows.anchor: لتكونوا على رجاء من أن تقربوا من النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive 'he was called' leaves the caller implicit because the end of the preceding speech already makes clear that God is the caller.
rows.anchor: دلالة واضحة على أن المننادي هو الله سبحانه , بنى للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's call is unlike ordinary speech and can be heard from every direction, while a place may be specially honored as the first place heard or where Moses stands.
rows.anchor: نداؤه سبحانه لا يشبه نداء غيره بل يكون من جميع الجوانب

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayri says there is consensus that Moses heard God's speech that night; if the tree had spoken, it would have been the speaker.
rows.anchor: قال القشيري : ومحصل الإجماع أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام سمع تلك الليلة كلام الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tree did not speak: God himself truly spoke to Moses, who heard him while in or by the blessed tree.
rows.anchor: وهو المتكلم سبحانه لا الشجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address turns from stubborn disbelievers to believers who are listening; the intimate singular address honors them, while even verbal faith with a small measure of inward assent falls under 'those who believe.'
rows.anchor: فشرفهم بالإضافة , ولكنه لما أشار بأداة البعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the surah came in Mecca while believers hid their worship and feared persecution, God emphasizes that the earth is wide in place, provision, and relief; those blocked from worship should migrate somewhere safer.
rows.anchor: مستخفين بالعبادة خوفا من الكفار , وكانت الهجرة الأهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship God alone in a place where it can be practiced fully, without compromise in speech or action or obedience to persecutors.
rows.anchor: أي خاصة بالهجرة إلى ارض تأمنون فيها اعبدوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Death separates everyone from all familiar things, even the body; contemplating death makes emigration easier, since obedience neither shortens life nor sin lengthens it.
rows.anchor: فإن أطاعت ربها أنجت نفسها ولم تنقصها الطاعة في الأجل شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everyone returns to God, not another, and is repaid for what they did.
rows.anchor: على عظمتنا , لا إلى غيرنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though the passage could describe punishment for defective faith, it omits that warning because the immediate aim is to encourage belief in any measure, and promises believers who do good deeds elevated rooms in Paradise.
rows.anchor: وكان القصد هنا الترغيب في الإيمان كيفما كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's promise to lodge the believers in gardens is emphatic; Hamza and al-Kisa'i read the verb with thāʾ from thawa, meaning to dwell.
rows.anchor: وقريب من هذا المعنى قراءةة حمزة والكسائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gardens' tall rooms overlook rivers, orchards, fields, and flowers; their residents remain forever without any discomfort prompting them to leave.
rows.anchor: أنهار , إلا كان به بساتين كبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reward is excellent, and its workers are defined by enduring patience through difficult duties such as migration until patience becomes their settled character.
rows.anchor: أوجدوا هذه الحقيقة حتى استقرت عندهم فكانت سجية لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They rely only on their Lord, renewing their trust in him in every matter, including provision after migration and struggle against enemies, rather than depending on family or homeland.
rows.anchor: أي وحده لا على أهل ولا وطن
